about: Engines beside the screen (DESIGN 5.12, N5): an engine declared `beside the screen` runs where its canvas is drawn (`canvas ... runs Screen`), one instance per canvas, from when its window opens until it closes. It speaks the engine interface of conformance/engines.json and exports `clarity_tick` and `clarity_draw` besides it. At every frame the renderer calls `clarity_tick` with the milliseconds since the last frame (`[ms]`; the first frame gives 0), then `clarity_draw` (`[]`), whose value is the canvas's shapes in its units, as a draw handler's (conformance/drawing.json). With `on open` (`opens`), `clarity_open` runs once, when the instance is made, before the first frame. The renderer skips a frame while the engine is still busy with the last one, so frames never pile up. `engine` is screen.wasm, built from engines/screen: it draws a dot that moves 1 unit every 10 ms and the time it has run. `frames` gives the ticks in order and the shapes after each. A frame that fails, or runs longer than the engine's time limit, ends the engine: the canvas shows `fails` in place of its drawing, the renderer calls it no more, and the window works on. `fails` cases give the ticks before and the tick that fails. Pointer and keys on the canvas go to the engine when it exports `clarity_pointer` and `clarity_key` (each is optional; without it the renderer sends none of that). The renderer keeps what happens between frames and hands it over at the start of the next frame, in order, before `clarity_tick`: `clarity_pointer` takes `[kind, x, y]`, kind `down`, `move` or `up`, in the canvas's units rounded down as a click is (conformance/drawing.json); `clarity_key` takes `[kind, key]`, kind `down` or `up`. `down` is the primary button or a touch going down on the drawing; while it is down the canvas keeps the pointer, so `move` and `up` beside the drawing are at its nearest edge (`near`). `move` is sent while the pointer is over the drawing or down. Moves in a row keep only the last (`queued`). A key is sent once when it goes down, not again while it repeats, and once when it comes up; when the canvas loses the keyboard, every key still down comes up. Only the keys of `keys` are sent, by those names: a letter as itself in lower case, a digit, and the named keys. `input` gives each frame's input, its ticks and the shapes after: screen.wasm moves its dot to where the pointer went down and drags it while down, and says which keys are down.
